study.title: The Love That Gives (four passages)
study.focus: What does God's gift of his Son tell us about the heart of God?
study.take: This take is the shortest shape: four passages, with Augustine's note covering both 3:17 and 3:18. The passages chosen here converge on the main line: God gives the Son to rescue (3:16), Christ comes to heal rather than condemn (3:17), and the one who believes is not condemned (3:18).
study.question: Christ came to heal, not to condemn. What does believing in him look like for you this week?
study.closing: The passages in this study point the same way: the Son was given to rescue, and the one who believes is not condemned. The gift is already offered; believing is how it is received.

scripture.16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
scripture.17: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
scripture.18: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.

summaries.MHC3.16.05: Matthew Henry marvels that the holy God would love so wicked a world with good will. Against the idea that the Messiah came only for one nation, he says Christ came in love to the whole world, Gentiles as well as Jews.
summaries.CHR3.16.1.01: Chrysostom hears Jesus saying: do not be shocked that I must be lifted up to save you. The Father loved you enough to give his Son for slaves, ungrateful ones, something a person would hardly do even for a friend.
summaries.AUG3.17-18.1.01: Augustine pictures Christ as a physician who came to heal the sick. He came to save the world, not to judge it; whoever refuses the physician's orders destroys himself and is judged by himself.
summaries.MHC3.18.01: Matthew Henry says a believer, though a great sinner who stands convicted, is not condemned. This is more than a delay: judgment is stopped, and he is acquitted and discharged.
